$$\begin{align*}2\sin^2\theta-\sin\theta-1&=0\\(2\sin\theta+1)(\sin\theta-1)&=0\end{align*}$$
By the null factor law, $\sin\theta=-\tfrac12$ or $\sin\theta=1$.

For $\sin\theta=-\tfrac12$, $A=\sin^{-1}(\tfrac12)=30^{\circ}$. Sine is negative in Q3 and Q4, so $\theta=180^{\circ}+30^{\circ}=210^{\circ}$ or $360^{\circ}-30^{\circ}=330^{\circ}$.

For $\sin\theta=1$, $\theta=90^{\circ}$.

Thus $\theta=90^{\circ},210^{\circ},330^{\circ}$.

$$\begin{align*}\tan^2\theta-\sqrt3\tan\theta&=0\\\tan\theta(\tan\theta-\sqrt3)&=0\end{align*}$$
By the null factor law, $\tan\theta=0$ or $\tan\theta=\sqrt3$.

For $\tan\theta=0$, $\theta=0^{\circ}$ or $180^{\circ}$.

For $\tan\theta=\sqrt3$, $A=\tan^{-1}(\sqrt3)=60^{\circ}$. Tangent is positive in Q1 and Q3, so $\theta=60^{\circ}$ or $180^{\circ}+60^{\circ}=240^{\circ}$.

Thus $\theta=0^{\circ},60^{\circ},180^{\circ},240^{\circ}$.

$$\begin{align*}2\sin^2\theta+\sin\theta-3&=0\\(2\sin\theta+3)(\sin\theta-1)&=0\end{align*}$$
By the null factor law, $\sin\theta=-\tfrac32$ or $\sin\theta=1$.

Since $-1\le\sin\theta\le1$, $\sin\theta=-\tfrac32$ has no solution.

For $\sin\theta=1$, $\theta=90^{\circ}$.

If the question doesn’t tell you whether a triangle has an acute or obtuse angle:

1. Use the sine rule to find the acute angle $\theta$. If $\sin\theta>1$, no triangle exists.
2. Find the obtuse angle $\theta'=180^\circ-\theta$.
3. Add each of $\theta$ and $\theta'$ to the given angle (the angle opposite the other known side). Reject any value whose sum is $\ge 180^\circ$ (the third angle must be greater than $0^\circ$).
